name: Lie algebra homomorphism
description: A linear map φ: g → h between Lie algebras satisfying φ([x,y]) = [φ(x),φ(y)] for all x,y in g.

name: Lie subalgebra
description: A vector subspace h of a Lie algebra g that is closed under the Lie bracket, i.e., [h,h] ⊆ h.

name: Ideal of a Lie algebra
description: A Lie subalgebra a of g such that [g,a] ⊆ a, making it the kernel of some Lie algebra homomorphism.

name: Quotient Lie algebra
description: For an ideal a of g, the vector space g/a equipped with the bracket [x+a, y+a] = [x,y]+a, yielding a well-defined Lie algebra structure.

name: Center of a Lie algebra
description: The ideal z(g) = {x ∈ g : [x,y] = 0 for all y ∈ g}, consisting of elements that bracket trivially with all of g.

name: Derived subalgebra (commutator subalgebra)
description: The ideal [g,g] = D(g) spanned by all brackets [x,y], measuring the failure of g to be abelian.

name: Derived series
description: The descending sequence D⁰(g) = g, Dⁿ⁺¹(g) = [Dⁿ(g), Dⁿ(g)] obtained by iterating the derived subalgebra construction.

name: Abelian Lie algebra
description: A Lie algebra g in which [x,y] = 0 for all x,y, equivalently g = z(g), so the bracket is identically zero.

name: Solvable Lie algebra
description: A Lie algebra g whose derived series terminates at zero, i.e., Dⁿ(g) = 0 for some n, generalizing commutativity in a hierarchical sense.

name: Nilpotent Lie algebra
description: A Lie algebra g whose lower central series terminates at zero, i.e., Cⁿ(g) = 0 for some n, meaning iterated bracketing with g eventually kills everything.

name: Radical of a Lie algebra
description: The unique maximal solvable ideal rad(g) of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra g, which contains every solvable ideal.

name: Simple Lie algebra
description: A non-abelian Lie algebra whose only ideals are 0 and itself, serving as the irreducible building blocks of semisimple Lie algebras.

name: Lie's theorem
description: If g is a solvable Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and V is a finite-dimensional g-module, then there exists a common eigenvector for all elements of g acting on V.

name: Cartan's criterion for solvability
description: A finite-dimensional Lie algebra g over a field of characteristic zero is solvable if and only if B(x,y) = 0 for all x ∈ g and y ∈ [g,g], where B is the Killing form.

name: Cartan's criterion for semisimplicity
description: A finite-dimensional Lie algebra g over a field of characteristic zero is semisimple if and only if its Killing form is non-degenerate.

name: Levi decomposition
description: Every finite-dimensional Lie algebra g over a field of characteristic zero is a semidirect product g = rad(g) ⋊ s where s is a semisimple subalgebra (called a Levi factor), and any two Levi factors are conjugate.

name: Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt theorem
description: If {x₁,...,xₙ} is an ordered basis of g, then the monomials x₁^{a₁}···xₙ^{aₙ} form a basis of U(g), proving the canonical map g → U(g) is injective.

name: Normalizer of a subalgebra
description: For a subalgebra h of g, the subalgebra N_g(h) = {x ∈ g : [x,h] ⊆ h}, the largest subalgebra of g in which h is an ideal.

name: Centralizer in a Lie algebra
description: For a subset S of g, the subalgebra C_g(S) = {x ∈ g : [x,s] = 0 for all s ∈ S}, consisting of elements commuting with all of S.

name: Semidirect product of Lie algebras
description: Given Lie algebras h and a with a representation ρ: h → der(a), the vector space h ⊕ a with bracket [(h₁,a₁),(h₂,a₂)] = ([h₁,h₂], [a₁,a₂]+ρ(h₁)a₂−ρ(h₂)a₁).

name: Derivation of a Lie algebra
description: A linear map D: g → g satisfying D([x,y]) = [D(x),y] + [x,D(y)], with inner derivations being those of the form ad(x).

name: Whitehead's lemma (first)
description: For a semisimple Lie algebra g over a field of characteristic zero and a finite-dimensional g-module V, every derivation from g to V is inner, i.e., H¹(g,V) = 0.

name: Whitehead's lemma (second)
description: For a semisimple Lie algebra g over characteristic zero and a finite-dimensional g-module V, every extension of g by V splits, i.e., H²(g,V) = 0.

name: Jordan decomposition in a Lie algebra
description: In a semisimple Lie algebra g over a perfect field, each element x has a unique decomposition x = xₛ + xₙ with xₛ semisimple, xₙ nilpotent, and [xₛ,xₙ] = 0, compatible with any faithful representation.

name: Invariant bilinear form
description: A bilinear form B on g satisfying B([x,y],z) = B(x,[y,z]) for all x,y,z ∈ g, with the Killing form being the canonical example.

name: Free Lie algebra
description: The Lie algebra L(X) freely generated by a set X, characterized by the universal property that any map X → g to a Lie algebra extends uniquely to a homomorphism L(X) → g.

name: Witt formula
description: The dimension of the degree-n homogeneous component of the free Lie algebra on q generators is (1/n)∑_{d|n} μ(d)q^{n/d}, where μ is the Möbius function.

name: Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formula
description: For elements x,y in a complete filtered Lie algebra (or in a neighborhood of identity in a Lie group), log(eˣeʸ) = x + y + ½[x,y] + 1/12([x,[x,y]]+[y,[y,x]]) + ···, expressing the group product in terms of iterated Lie brackets.

name: Lie group homomorphism
description: A smooth group homomorphism between Lie groups, whose differential at the identity is a Lie algebra homomorphism.

name: Lie algebra of a Lie group
description: The tangent space at the identity g = T_eG equipped with the Lie bracket inherited from left-invariant vector fields, functorially associated to the Lie group G.

name: Lie subgroup
description: A subgroup H of a Lie group G that is an immersed submanifold (or, in the closed case, an embedded submanifold) carrying an induced Lie group structure.

name: Closed subgroup theorem (Cartan's theorem)
description: Every closed subgroup of a Lie group is an embedded Lie subgroup, i.e., it automatically inherits a smooth manifold structure making it a Lie group in the subspace topology.

name: Quotient of a Lie group
description: For a closed normal subgroup N of G, the quotient G/N carries a unique Lie group structure making the projection G → G/N a smooth surjective homomorphism with Lie algebra g/n.

name: Lie functor
description: The functor Lie: LieGrp → LieAlg sending each Lie group to its Lie algebra and each homomorphism to its differential at the identity, providing the algebraic linearization of group theory.

name: Integration of Lie algebra homomorphisms
description: The process of lifting a Lie algebra homomorphism g → h to a Lie group homomorphism G → H when G is simply connected, by using the exponential map and path-lifting.

name: Coxeter group
description: A group W with a presentation ⟨s₁,...,sₙ | (sᵢsⱼ)^{mᵢⱼ} = 1⟩ where mᵢᵢ = 1 and mᵢⱼ = mⱼᵢ ≥ 2 (or ∞), abstracting the structure of reflection groups.

name: Coxeter matrix
description: A symmetric matrix M = (mᵢⱼ) with mᵢᵢ = 1 and mᵢⱼ ∈ {2,3,...,∞} for i≠j, encoding the orders of products of pairs of generators in a Coxeter group.

name: Coxeter graph
description: A labeled graph with vertices indexed by generators of a Coxeter group, edges connecting pairs with mᵢⱼ ≥ 3, and edge labels mᵢⱼ when mᵢⱼ ≥ 4, encoding the Coxeter matrix.

name: Exchange property
description: In a Coxeter group, if ℓ(sw) < ℓ(w) for a simple reflection s, then there exists an index i such that sw = s₁···ŝᵢ···sₖ (omitting sᵢ) for any reduced expression w = s₁···sₖ.

name: Deletion property
description: In a Coxeter group, any non-reduced expression s₁···sₖ can be shortened by deleting an even number of factors to obtain a reduced expression for the same element.

name: Tits system (BN-pair)
description: A group G with subgroups B and N such that B ∩ N = T is normal in N, W = N/T is a Coxeter group with generators S, and the axioms BwB·BsB ⊆ BwsB ∪ BwB and sBs⁻¹ ⊄ B hold for all w ∈ W, s ∈ S.

name: Parabolic subgroup of a Coxeter group
description: For a subset J ⊆ S of simple reflections, the subgroup W_J generated by J, which is itself a Coxeter group with Coxeter matrix restricted to J.

name: Coxeter complex
description: The simplicial complex associated to a Coxeter group W whose simplices are cosets of parabolic subgroups of W, serving as the building block (apartment) of a Tits building.

name: Matsumoto's theorem
description: Any two reduced expressions for the same element of a Coxeter group are related by a sequence of braid relations sᵢsⱼsᵢ··· = sⱼsᵢsⱼ··· (mᵢⱼ factors each side), without requiring insertion/deletion.

name: Strong exchange property
description: In a Coxeter group, if ℓ(tw) < ℓ(w) for a reflection t (not necessarily simple), then t can replace one of the factors in any reduced expression for w.

name: Classification of finite Coxeter groups
description: The irreducible finite Coxeter groups are exactly the types Aₙ, Bₙ, Dₙ, E₆, E₇, E₈, F₄, G₂ (crystallographic, i.e., Weyl groups) together with H₃, H₄, and I₂(m) (non-crystallographic).

name: Coroot
description: For a root α, the coroot α∨ = 2α/⟨α,α⟩, such that the reflection s_α(β) = β − ⟨β,α∨⟩α, and the coroots form the dual root system.

name: Cartan matrix
description: The n×n integer matrix A = (aᵢⱼ) where aᵢⱼ = ⟨αᵢ,αⱼ∨⟩ for simple roots αᵢ,αⱼ, satisfying aᵢᵢ = 2, aᵢⱼ ≤ 0 for i≠j, and aᵢⱼ = 0 iff aⱼᵢ = 0, determining the root system up to isomorphism.

name: Classification of irreducible root systems
description: The connected Dynkin diagrams (equivalently irreducible root systems) are exactly Aₙ (n≥1), Bₙ (n≥2), Cₙ (n≥3), Dₙ (n≥4), E₆, E₇, E₈, F₄, and G₂.

name: Weyl chamber
description: A connected component of E \ ∪_{α∈Φ} H_α where H_α = ker(α), forming a fundamental domain for the W-action; the dominant chamber is the one defined by ⟨·,αᵢ∨⟩ > 0 for all simple αᵢ.

name: Root lattice
description: The Z-span Q = ZΦ of the root system in E, a sublattice of the weight lattice, with the quotient P/Q being a finite group isomorphic to the center of the simply connected group.

name: Fundamental weights
description: The basis {ω₁,...,ωₙ} of the weight lattice P dual to the simple coroots, defined by ⟨ωᵢ,αⱼ∨⟩ = δᵢⱼ, indexing the vertices of the fundamental Weyl chamber.

name: Extended (affine) Dynkin diagram
description: The Dynkin diagram augmented by an additional node corresponding to the negative of the highest root −θ, classifying affine root systems and appearing in the theory of loop algebras.

name: Affine root system
description: An infinite root system on an affine space obtained by adding integer translates α + nδ of roots of a finite root system, whose Weyl group is the affine Weyl group acting by reflections in affine hyperplanes.

name: Affine Weyl group
description: The infinite Coxeter group generated by reflections in affine hyperplanes H_{α,n} = {x : ⟨x,α⟩ = n}, isomorphic to the semidirect product W ⋉ Q∨ of the Weyl group with the coroot lattice.

name: Alcove
description: A connected component of the complement of all affine reflecting hyperplanes, forming a fundamental domain for the affine Weyl group; the fundamental alcove is a simplex.

name: Root space decomposition
description: For a semisimple Lie algebra g with Cartan subalgebra h, the decomposition g = h ⊕ (⊕_{α∈Φ} g_α) where g_α = {x ∈ g : [h,x] = α(h)x for all h ∈ h} and Φ ⊂ h* is the root system.

name: Chevalley basis
description: A basis {hᵢ, e_α} of a semisimple Lie algebra with integer structure constants, consisting of coroots hᵢ = αᵢ∨ in h and root vectors e_α ∈ g_α satisfying [e_α, e_{-α}] = α∨ and specific sign conventions.

name: Conjugacy of Cartan subalgebras
description: Any two Cartan subalgebras of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero are conjugate by an inner automorphism of g.

name: sl₂-triple
description: A triple (e,h,f) in a Lie algebra satisfying [h,e] = 2e, [h,f] = −2f, [e,f] = h, spanning a subalgebra isomorphic to sl(2), with one such triple for each root.

name: Jacobson-Morozov theorem
description: In a semisimple Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero, every nilpotent element e can be embedded in an sl₂-triple (e,h,f), and the sl₂-triples for a given nilpotent orbit are conjugate.

name: Split semisimple Lie algebra
description: A semisimple Lie algebra g over a field k possessing a splitting Cartan subalgebra h such that all roots are in k (not just in the algebraic closure), equivalently g is an inner form.

name: Parabolic subalgebra
description: A subalgebra p of g containing a Borel subalgebra, classified by subsets of simple roots and corresponding to parabolic subgroups in the group setting.

name: Kostant multiplicity formula
description: The multiplicity of weight μ in L(λ) is dim L(λ)_μ = ∑_{w∈W} ε(w) P(w(λ+ρ) − (μ+ρ)) where P is the Kostant partition function counting expressions as sums of positive roots.

name: Kostant partition function
description: The function P(ν) counting the number of ways to write ν as an unordered sum of positive roots (with repetition), appearing in weight multiplicity formulas.

name: Freudenthal's formula
description: A recursive formula computing the multiplicity of a weight μ in L(λ) using the inner product of weights and the multiplicities of higher weights, derived from the Casimir operator.

name: Existence theorem for semisimple Lie algebras
description: For every Cartan matrix (equivalently every Dynkin diagram), there exists a unique (up to isomorphism) semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero having that Cartan matrix.

name: Serre's presentation (Serre relations)
description: A semisimple Lie algebra is the quotient of the free Lie algebra on generators {eᵢ, fᵢ, hᵢ} by the relations [hᵢ,hⱼ]=0, [hᵢ,eⱼ]=aᵢⱼeⱼ, [hᵢ,fⱼ]=−aᵢⱼfⱼ, [eᵢ,fⱼ]=δᵢⱼhᵢ, and (ad eᵢ)^{1−aᵢⱼ}(eⱼ)=0 (and similarly for f).

name: Maximal torus
description: A maximal connected abelian subgroup T of a compact Lie group G, isomorphic to (S¹)ʳ where r = rank(G); every element of G is conjugate to an element of T.

name: Conjugacy of maximal tori
description: Any two maximal tori in a compact Lie group are conjugate by an inner automorphism, so the rank and the Weyl group N_G(T)/T are well-defined invariants.

name: Compact real form
description: A compact real Lie subalgebra g_u of a complex semisimple Lie algebra g_C such that g_C = g_u ⊗_R C, unique up to conjugacy; its Killing form is negative definite.

name: Weyl's unitary trick
description: The technique of proving results for a complex semisimple Lie algebra by passing to its compact real form, where integration over the compact group via Haar measure and averaging yields complete reducibility and other results.

name: Banach algebra
description: A complete normed algebra A over C (or R) satisfying ‖xy‖ ≤ ‖x‖·‖y‖, providing the analytic framework for spectral theory and operator algebras.

name: Spectral radius formula (Gelfand's formula)
description: In a Banach algebra, the spectral radius satisfies r(a) = lim_{n→∞} ‖aⁿ‖^{1/n} = inf_{n≥1} ‖aⁿ‖^{1/n}, providing a formula for the spectral radius purely in terms of the norm.

name: Resolvent identity
description: For λ,μ in the resolvent set, R(λ,a) − R(μ,a) = (μ−λ)R(λ,a)R(μ,a), and the resolvent is an analytic function of λ vanishing at infinity.

name: Character (multiplicative linear functional)
description: A nonzero algebra homomorphism χ: A → C from a commutative Banach algebra A, necessarily continuous with ‖χ‖ = 1 and χ(1) = 1, forming the points of the Gelfand spectrum.

name: Gelfand spectrum (maximal ideal space)
description: The set Ω(A) of all characters of a commutative unital Banach algebra A, equipped with the weak-* topology making it a compact Hausdorff space; maximal ideals correspond bijectively to characters via ker(χ).

name: C*-identity
description: The norm condition ‖a*a‖ = ‖a‖² characterizing C*-algebras, from which it follows that ‖a*‖ = ‖a‖ and the norm is uniquely determined by the algebraic structure.

name: State on a C*-algebra
description: A positive linear functional φ: A → C with ‖φ‖ = 1 (or φ(1) = 1 in the unital case), serving as a noncommutative probability measure and providing the input for the GNS construction.

name: Cyclic vector
description: A vector ξ in a Hilbert space H such that π(A)ξ is dense in H for a representation π of A, ensuring the representation is determined by the state φ(a) = ⟨π(a)ξ,ξ⟩.

name: Spectral mapping theorem
description: For a continuous function f and a normal element a of a C*-algebra, σ(f(a)) = f(σ(a)), so the spectrum of f(a) is the image of the spectrum of a under f.

name: Unitization of a C*-algebra
description: For a non-unital C*-algebra A, the C*-algebra Ã = A ⊕ C with multiplication (a,λ)(b,μ) = (ab+λb+μa, λμ) and a suitable norm making it a unital C*-algebra containing A as a maximal ideal.

name: Locally compact group
description: A topological group whose underlying topology is locally compact and Hausdorff, providing the natural setting for abstract harmonic analysis with the existence of Haar measure.

name: Convolution product
description: The binary operation (f*g)(x) = ∫_G f(y)g(y⁻¹x)dy on L¹(G), making it a Banach algebra; for abelian groups, the Gelfand transform of L¹(G) is the Fourier transform.

name: Modular function
description: The continuous homomorphism Δ: G → R₊* relating left and right Haar measures by d(μ_right) = Δ(g)d(μ_left), with G unimodular when Δ ≡ 1 (e.g., compact, abelian, or semisimple groups).

name: Group C*-algebra C*(G)
description: The completion of L¹(G) with respect to the norm ‖f‖_{C*} = sup_π ‖π(f)‖ where the supremum is over all *-representations of L¹(G), whose representations correspond bijectively to unitary representations of G.

name: Spectral theorem for bounded normal operators
description: For a bounded normal operator T on a Hilbert space, there exists a unique spectral measure E on σ(T) such that T = ∫_{σ(T)} λ dE(λ), establishing a bijection between normal operators and spectral measures on compact subsets of C.

name: Spectral theorem for commuting normal operators
description: A finite family of pairwise commuting bounded normal operators on a Hilbert space has a joint spectral measure E on the product of their spectra, simultaneously diagonalizing all operators as T_k = ∫ λ_k dE(λ₁,...,λₙ).

name: SNAG theorem (Stone-Naimark-Ambrose-Godement)
description: Every strongly continuous unitary representation of a locally compact abelian group G on a Hilbert space is of the form π(g) = ∫_Ĝ χ(g) dE(χ) for a unique spectral measure E on the Pontryagin dual Ĝ.

name: Type decomposition of von Neumann algebras
description: Every von Neumann algebra decomposes uniquely as a direct sum of type I, type II₁, type II_∞, and type III factors, classified by the structure of their projection lattices.

name: Holomorphic functional calculus
description: For an element a of a unital Banach algebra and f holomorphic on a neighborhood of σ(a), f(a) = (1/2πi)∮_Γ f(λ)(λ−a)⁻¹dλ defines an algebra homomorphism from the algebra of germs of holomorphic functions on σ(a) to A.

name: Fell topology
description: The topology on the set of irreducible representations of a C*-algebra (or locally compact group) defined by convergence of states, making the unitary dual a (generally non-Hausdorff) topological space.

name: Spectral permanence
description: If B is a closed *-subalgebra of a C*-algebra A and a ∈ B, then σ_B(a) = σ_A(a); the spectrum of an element does not change when computed in a C*-subalgebra.
